one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent lacks sufficient CoreWars domain knowledge to design warriors that achieve the required win rates, and then spends 480+ steps repeating minor cosmetic variations of fundamentally identical failing designs without ever discovering a working strategy.
t_err_evidence: Step 10: agent writes first real warrior attempt using a scanner design with spl instructions to large offsets like >1000, >2000 etc. that do not implement the needed bombing/scanning strategy; the agent acts on the false premise that adding SPL instructions with large B-field offsets will create useful process splitting and that a simple 3-instruction scanner loop will beat Stone and Paper at 75%+ win rate.
t_commit_evidence: Step 13: first real test results show catastrophic failure across all opponents (Stone: 28%, Paper: 27%, Vampire: 57%, Snake: 0%, G2-Clear: 0%). The agent thereafter doubles down on minor variations of the same flawed scan-and-bomb architecture for the remaining 479 steps, never fundamentally rethinking.
t_surface_evidence: Step 13: explicit test output shows Dwarf Scanner scores 85 vs Stone's 214, Paper's 73 vs Dwarf's 154, etc. all falling far short of the required win rates, making failure observable.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the CoreWars domain knowledge needed to design warriors capable of meeting the performance thresholds. It does not understand how to: (1) beat fast scanners like Stone with a replicator that actually works; (2) beat Paper with a proper and faster replicator; (3) beat Snake and G2-Clear with targeted strategies. Instead, it generates syntactically plausible but strategically ineffective redcode that cycles through the same three design patterns (scanner/bomber/hybrid) with minor parameter tweaks, never achieving the target win rates.
forewarning_evidence: Step 8: the first test script run produces empty output for all opponents (pmars -b -r 100 -f my_warrior.red gives no scores/wins), signaling that the initial warrior test setup is broken before the agent pivots to testing the 'Dwarf Scanner' design.
